t: The contraception toolbox and its warning labels
story: Open the toolbox: every tool wears a warning label. The pill, patch and ring carry a **red clot** label, because estrogen makes the liver bake extra clotting factors, so a smoker over 35 or anyone with migraine with aura leaves them on the shelf. **Rifampin** is a rifle that shoots the hormones out of the blood. The depot shot sends the ovaries into **winter**: no periods, thin bones and a slow spring thaw. The **matchstick** rod in the arm sputters with unpredictable spotting. The levonorgestrel IUD is a **dimmer** that fades the periods, while the copper IUD is a **leaky pipe** with heavier, crampier ones. The **raincoat** is the only tool that also stops infection. The **dome hat** left in too long brings toxic shock, and a **knotted tube** that fails sends the egg to the wrong address: an ectopic pregnancy.
keys: Estrogen in the pill, patch and ring raises clotting factors: venous and arterial clots. Avoid with smoking over 35 or migraine with aura.
Rifampin and other CYP3A4 enzyme inducers lower hormone levels; amoxicillin does not. Choose DMPA or an IUD instead.
DMPA every 3 months suppresses ovulation so strongly that estradiol stays low: amenorrhea, bone density loss and slow return of fertility.
The etonogestrel implant is the most effective reversible method but causes unpredictable spotting.
The levonorgestrel IUD thins the endometrium, so periods lighten or stop. It treats heavy menstrual bleeding.
The copper IUD has no hormone and works for 10 years or more, but periods often become heavier and more painful.
Condoms are the only method that also lowers the risk of infection.
The diaphragm with spermicide brings more urinary tract infections, and toxic shock syndrome if left in too long.
Tubal sterilization is permanent, but when it fails the pregnancy is more often ectopic.
